items.note: In all three samples the newsletter form sits in an outlined block on paper. The input gets a red border, and under it a red circle icon with the words 'Enter a valid email address, like name@example.com' says what went wrong and how to fix it. Subscribe is pink in sample 1 and ink in samples 2 and 3; nothing overlaps.

In dark mode the newsletter card is raised on a black ground. The red input border and the red icon plus message stay readable. Subscribe is pink in sample 1 and paper-filled in samples 2 and 3, the correct dark mapping for ink buttons, and the error text keeps its contrast.

At phone width the form stacks into one column: label, red-bordered input, a full-width pink (sample 1) or ink (samples 2 and 3) Subscribe button, then the icon and the two-line error message. Nothing is clipped, and the button stays in the page flow.

The form is replaced by a pink check icon and 'Thanks for subscribing. New posts will arrive at reader@example.com', inside the outlined block (samples 1 and 3) or inline beside the heading (sample 2). The outcome and the next thing to expect are both clear, and status is not shown by colour alone.
The same inline confirmation sits on the raised dark card. The pink check and paper text read clearly on black, and no toast or layer covers the footer or any control.
On mobile the check icon and the two-line thank-you message replace the field and button inside the block. The text wraps cleanly, the footer note follows below, and nothing overlaps.

The search field shows 'zzzz no match' with the pink focus halo, and 'Showing 0 of 6 posts' sits under it. Below is one magnifier sticker (pink handle, or yellow lens in sample 3), 'No posts match these filters', a hint line and a Clear filters lift button, pink in sample 1 and ink in samples 2 and 3, inside an outlined panel in samples 2 and 3.

In dark mode the empty panel is raised on black and the magnifier sticker keeps its ink-on-paper look. The message and hint are readable, and Clear filters is pink (sample 1) or paper-filled (samples 2 and 3), so the recovery action stays obvious.

At 390px the search field keeps its halo and clear ×, the filter pills scroll off the edge as a strip, and the sticker, 'No posts match these filters' and a full Clear filters button stack centred. Nothing is cut off.

Focus is on the ink current-page 'Home' pill in the header, which shows an extra outline ring around it. The rest of the page (yellow or periwinkle band hero, outlined post cards, newsletter block) stays at rest, and there is no browser-default blue ring.
In dark mode the focused 'Home' pill is paper-filled, and a pink ring with a clear gap around it marks focus. It stands out clearly against the black header.
On mobile the focused 'Home' pill shows a doubled ink outline ring in the header. It is readable and doesn't overlap the 'About' link next to it, and the page below is unchanged.

The hero stickers are flat shapes with heavy ink outlines and token fills: pink coins with an extruded paper or yellow rim and a heavy glyph, tilted arrows, stars, a pencil, speech bubbles, a tag and stacked cards or sheets. Each is a different object, they are cropped at the band edge like the reference's tilted coins, and none uses a gradient.

Each sample's article figure is an original sticker scene that fits the caption about grouping buttons: outlined boards holding pink, yellow and teal bars, with a small star accent in samples 2 and 3. Strokes are even and fills come from the band and pink tokens; the frame is yellow in samples 1 and 3 and paper in sample 2.

Each figure reads as 'the same release, rewritten for readers': a dense note or bubble, an arrow, then a shorter one. Sample 2 strikes out the left sheet in pink and puts a star on a periwinkle sheet. All are built from basic outlined shapes, readable at their size and as well made as the reference's sticker art.

The frames show the hero stickers moving at different speeds over the scroll (the coin, arrow and star shift between frames) without passing over the title or CTA. Sample 3 also shows the linear tag-wall marquee strip under the band. There is no bounce, scale or fade, and only the tag wall loops, which the spec allows as slow linear decoration.
